newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Dovrat Shrem raises $50 mln for Israeli fund.
newsitem.headline: Dovrat Shrem raises $50 mln for Israeli fund.

text.p: Israel's Dovrat Shrem Group said on Monday it has completed the first round of funding for the Polaris II venture capital fund, raising about $50 million from foreign and Israeli investors.
The fund is expected to reach $100 million, with an additional $25 million raised this year.
The Dovrat Shrem Group founded the Polaris Fund II together with the investment bank Cowen & Co and the Travelers Group, which owns Smith Barney.
The fund intends to invest in technology intensive companies with an Israeli nexus in the areas of communications, software, electronics, biotechnology and medicine, among others.

The first stage of fundraising was completed in three months. The fund's foreign investors include Travelers Group, Cowen & Co, Claridge Israel -- an investment vehicle of Canadian businessman Charles Bronfman -- and BEA, the manager of the Israel Fund.
Among the Israeli investors are Arison Investments, Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, Bank Leumi, Ormat and Delek Investments, a subsidiary of the Delek the Israel Fuel Corp.
With the completion of the first round of financing for the fund, the Dovrat Shrem Group increased the venture capital funds under its management to $135 million.
